title: The Cake That Wasn't Ready
setting: You are at the counter of a neighborhood bakery. Avery was told a birthday cake for their father would be ready at 4:00. It is 4:50, and guests are already at the house.

nodes.speaker: Avery
nodes.text: I was told four o'clock. It's almost five, and people are already at my dad's house. Where is the cake?

choices.text: You're right to be upset. We said four, and we missed it.
choices.rationale: You named the broken promise before you explained the kitchen. Avery can tell the impact landed.

choices.text: We've been slammed all afternoon. Orders run late sometimes.
choices.rationale: A busy shift may be true, but it asks Avery to care about your problem before their own.

choices.text: I can have it boxed in twenty minutes.
choices.rationale: A time is useful, but you skipped the fact that guests are already waiting.

nodes.speaker: Avery
nodes.text: Okay. Thank you for saying that. I need to know what I can tell them.

choices.text: It's frosted. I'll box it, write the message, and have it in your hands in fifteen minutes.
choices.rationale: A specific next step and a time they can repeat to their family lowers the uncertainty.

choices.text: You have to understand how hard today has been on us, too.
choices.rationale: Turning the conversation back to your stress undoes the acknowledgment you just offered.

nodes.speaker: Avery
nodes.text: That doesn't help me. My dad thinks I forgot him.

choices.text: You're right. That was about us, not your dad. Fifteen minutes, and I'll walk it out.
choices.rationale: You repaired the brush-off and then gave a concrete plan. The order matters.

choices.text: I already told you we're busy. You'll get it when it's done.
choices.rationale: A second dismissal leaves Avery with nothing they can tell the people waiting.

nodes.speaker: Avery
nodes.text: Twenty minutes. What am I supposed to say when they ask why I don't have it?

choices.text: Tell them I missed the time I gave you, and that I'm sorry. Fifteen minutes, message written.
choices.rationale: You went back for the feeling and still left them with a sentence they can use.

choices.text: Just say it's on the way. That's the best I can do.
choices.rationale: You handed them a vague line and kept the apology for yourself.

nodes.speaker: Avery
nodes.text: Fifteen minutes. I can work with that. Please put 'Happy birthday, Dad' on the top.

choices.text: Happy birthday, Dad. I'll read it back to you when I bring the box out.
choices.rationale: Repeating the message shows you heard the detail, not only the complaint.

choices.text: Sure. I'll figure the wording out.
choices.rationale: The wording is the part they still have control over. Leaving it vague keeps them on edge.

nodes.speaker: Avery
nodes.text: Thank you. I'll tell them I'm walking out with it.

nodes.speaker: Avery
nodes.text: I'll wait. I'm not going to pretend this was fine.
